subject: research/ambient-ips
professional: a machine-learning researcher in off-policy / counterfactual learning and importance-weighted active learning (inverse-propensity, self-normalised and doubly robust estimators); first checks: does the fitting routine reach the estimator it claims, are the propensities the ones actually used to act, is the variance of 1/epsilon weights controlled (clipping, self-normalisation), and is the work positioned against Horvitz-Thompson, Beygelzimer, Dasgupta and Langford 2009 (IWAL), Strehl et al. 2010, Bottou et al. 2013 and Swaminathan and Joachims 2015

evidence.correctness: The pipeline reproduces (experiments/run.py rerun in a scratch copy: results.txt identical apart from the runtime line, 254 s) and the oracle reference is right: a closed-form Bayes posterior from the World defaults (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/cf8c4a25-3d1e-5701-a418-44569f367c15/scratchpad/ambient-ips/chk/analytic.py) gives weights [2.0, 2.242, 0, -5.991] against the code's [1.998, 2.263, -0.019, -6.002] and expected utility 12.52/h against the held-out 12.71 (std 0.58 over 20 streams). But fit_map (ips.py:46-64) is undamped Newton with no line search, and it diverges. An independent damped Newton with Armijo backtracking on the exact logaddexp objective (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/cf8c4a25-3d1e-5701-a418-44569f367c15/scratchpad/ambient-ips/chk/mysolver.py, mapcheck.py) on 24 hour-100 fits (2 priors x 2 eps x 2 weightings x seeds 0-2): all 6 uninformed unweighted fits and 3 of 12 IPS fits are non-converged, e.g. uninformed eps=0.002 none seed 0: J(code)=47,679 vs J(true MAP)=105.0, ||w-w0||=163 > the bound sqrt(2J(w0))=34.9 that any MAP must satisfy; uninformed eps=0.002 ips seed 0: J=526,416,828 vs 1,386.8, ||w-w0||=30,622. Rerunning the whole run.py with the converged solver (same seeds, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/cf8c4a25-3d1e-5701-a418-44569f367c15/scratchpad/ambient-ips/fixed, 197 s): all six uninformed rows equal the informed ones within 0.05 (online 9.65/7.79/8.48/8.13/2.65/3.17 against README -1.74/-19.34/-2.04/-26.27/-23.27/-30.53), the IPS stds of 35-44 drop to 1.0-3.7, informed eps=0.002 ips model@100h 6.74 +- 14.03 -> 9.62 +- 3.36, and drift IPS with 20 h memory -7.79 +- 13.85 -> -0.18 +- 2.16 (IPS without memory 0.68 -> 1.34, now the best online drift row). Result 1 and the 'worst row' part of result 4 are optimizer artifacts; results 2 and 3 survive.
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 5 tests pass (0.82 s), run.py reproduces results.txt, experiments/figure.py and ips_online.svg exist, the README table matches results.txt in all 12 rows (script parse, 0 mismatches), and the drift block matches. Clipping, self-normalisation, DR weights, decaying eps and real logs are listed as not done, not claimed.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests: 5 passed. 4 of 4 seeded mutants in core logic survived (propensity of explored windows set to 1 so IPS equals the unweighted fit; decision rule ignoring the others-talking cost; forget window doubled; prior gradient centred on zero). No test checks that fit_map's output is stationary or within the prior-distance bound, the check that would have caught the divergence; test_informed_ips_learns_most_of_oracle passes because the informed-prior eps=0.02 fits happen to converge.
evidence.craft: Read src/ambient_ips/ips.py, tests/test_ips.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Compact and readable, seeds fixed, figure parses results.txt rather than retyping. Defects: fit_map copied from ambient-bandit with the same undamped Newton (fixed in ambient-fullinfo by PR #18259 but not here); returned covariance is inv(H) at the pre-step iterate; sigmoid clipped at +-30 makes saturated points vanish from the Hessian, feeding the overshoot; run.py writes results.txt by relative path (must run from the project root).
evidence.claims: Checked: (a) 'Stylised, simulated results only' disclosure, README:3: backed. (b) 'Under this design the weighted log-likelihood ... same expectation as over all windows', README:21: sound (propensity known and logged per window; holds under adaptive data collection by iterated expectation). (c) Result 1 'IPS did not fix the uninformed-prior failure', README:50, and the homepage summary 'did not rescue the uninformed-prior ... scenarios' (research/_homepage/projects.json:1957): false, there is no uninformed-prior failure under a converged solver. (d) 'at eps=0.002 an explored window counts 500 times', README:50: 1/0.002 = 500, pass. (e) 'about 7 of the 360 hourly windows are explored' at eps=0.02, README:51: 0.02 x 360 = 7.2 upper bound, pass. (f) Result 4 'IPS with memory is the worst row (-7.79 +- 13.85)', README:53: artifact, -0.18 +- 2.16 converged. (g) 'selection bias matters little with these features', README:52: hedged guess, contradicted by ambient-fullinfo's measured 1.3-2.1 utility/h loss. (h) Horvitz-Thompson and Horvitz 1999 citations: bibliographic details match (JASA 47(260):663-685; CHI '99 159-166).
evidence.fitness: A researcher could not build on the headline result without first replacing the solver and rerunning. Nearest prior work: importance-weighted active learning (Beygelzimer, Dasgupta and Langford 2009, ICML), which is exactly 'query with known probability, weight by 1/probability' for a learner choosing its own labels; off-policy learning from logged bandit feedback (Strehl et al. 2010; Bottou et al. 2013 JMLR; Swaminathan and Joachims 2015 JMLR); truncated importance sampling for variance (Ionides 2008). None is cited. With the solver fixed, what remains (IPS unbiased but noisier at small eps; constant-eps exploration costs more than it teaches in this toy) is the textbook bias-variance trade-off of IPS, not new; the result is sound only after the fix, and the nearest sibling (ambient-fullinfo) already carries the corrected version.
evidence.domain: The IPS construction itself follows standard practice: per-window logged propensity, 1/pi weight on the log-likelihood, greedy windows propensity 1, explored windows eps, and a held-out no-exploration evaluation separating learning from exploration cost. Departures a practitioner would flag first: a non-convergent optimizer (any off-policy practitioner checks the weighted objective reached its minimum before comparing estimators), no clipped/self-normalised/DR baseline (admitted), no multiple-comparison handling (admitted), and the uninformed-prior 'failure' mechanism never diagnosed.

defects.what: fit_map is undamped Newton with no line search; it diverges from the uninformed prior start and on large-weight IPS fits (9 of 24 hour-100 fits checked: objective 450x to 380,000x the true minimum, ||w-w0|| 163 to 30,622 against a bound of 35-117). The online learner acts on these weights, so the logged history is distorted too. Same bug as ambient-fullinfo (fixed there by PR #18259) and ambient-bandit.

Result 1 ('IPS did not fix the uninformed-prior failure', stds 35-44), the informed eps=0.002 IPS row (6.74 +- 14.03) and 'IPS with memory is the worst row' in result 4 are optimizer artifacts: converged, uninformed rows equal informed rows, IPS stds are 1.0-3.7, and IPS with memory is -0.18 +- 2.16. The homepage summary repeats the uninformed-prior claim.

Core logic untested: 4 of 4 seeded mutants survived (explored propensity set to 1, so IPS = unweighted; decision rule ignoring the others cost; forget window doubled; prior gradient centred on zero). No test checks fit_map stationarity or the prior-distance bound.

Nearest prior work not cited and novelty not positioned: importance-weighted active learning (Beygelzimer, Dasgupta and Langford 2009) is the same query-with-known-probability, weight-by-1/p design; off-policy learning from logged bandit feedback (Strehl et al. 2010; Bottou et al. 2013; Swaminathan and Joachims 2015) and truncated IS (Ionides 2008) already establish the variance problem the README rediscovers.
The hedged guess 'the selection bias matters little with these features' is contradicted by the follow-up ambient-fullinfo (biased fit loses 1.3-2.1 utility/h) and the README does not point to it.

Copied engine: fit_map duplicated from ambient-bandit (and into ambient-fullinfo and others) so a fix in one leaves the rest broken; returned covariance is inv(H) at the pre-step iterate; run.py writes results.txt by relative path.

verdict: A tidy, reproducible stylised study (run.py regenerates results.txt exactly; the oracle weights and 12.7/h oracle utility match a closed-form Bayes computation; the IPS construction with logged propensities is textbook-correct) whose headline negative result is a solver bug. fit_map is undamped Newton copied from ambient-bandit; an independent line-searched solver shows 9 of 24 hour-100 fits are non-converged, including every uninformed unweighted fit. Rerun with a converged solver, the 'uninformed-prior failure' that IPS 'did not fix' does not exist (uninformed rows equal informed rows), IPS variance falls from std 35-44 to 1-4, and the drift 'worst row' (IPS with memory, -7.79) becomes -0.18. What survives (constant-eps exploration costs more than it teaches; IPS is noisier at small eps and helps model quality only at eps = 0.02) is the known IPS bias-variance trade-off, uncited against IWAL and the logged-bandit literature. 4 of 4 seeded mutants survived the 5 tests. Does not meet the bar; porting ambient-fullinfo's damped-Newton fit_map (PR #18259), adding a stationarity test, regenerating results.txt and rewriting results 1 and 4 would lift correctness and claims.
